sources.title: How HR Software Buying Logic Is Changing in 2026
sources.population: Mixed HR, IT, Finance and executive software-experienced respondents; geography not established
sources.locator: Study methodology and chapters 1–5; role mix and sponsorship disclosure
sources.summary: Buying logic, switching burden, total ownership cost and controls are already examined. The study uses AI-conducted voice interviews with real respondents and analyst-reviewed synthesis. Only 8% of the displayed role mix is Finance/Payroll; it is not a senior-payroll-only UK cohort.
sources.funding_or_commercial_interest: Commissioned by Paycom; publisher states editorial independence
sources.limitations: Relevant direct overlap, not proof of UK payroll prevalence or JGA buyer demand.
sources.publication_eligibility: Working context or source-attributed finding; final wording and rights checks pending

sources.title: G2 Research methodology
sources.population: General AICR method, not an additional respondent sample
sources.locator: Research design, recruitment, interview execution and synthesis sections
sources.summary: Explains AI-led interviews of real participants, screening and analyst review. This supplies method context for SRC-0060; it is not an independent corroborating dataset.
sources.funding_or_commercial_interest: Research provider describing its own method
sources.limitations: Do not copy its scale, recruitment claims or blinding into JGA's method.
sources.publication_eligibility: Working context or source-attributed finding; final wording and rights checks pending

sources.title: The Vistra Payroll Report 2026
sources.population: Payroll leaders at UK and US corporates
sources.locator: Printed pages 3, 5 and 10; pages 5 and 10 visually verified
sources.summary: The report already covers regulatory project delays, compliance-related technology barriers and provider-selection confidence. It reports both friction and confidence in providers. Sampling/recruitment details and question-level bases are not fully disclosed.
sources.funding_or_commercial_interest: Payroll-service provider publishing its own research
sources.limitations: A reported combined delay-or-change measure is not outright abandonment or a causal estimate of approval failure.
sources.publication_eligibility: Working context or source-attributed finding; final wording and rights checks pending

sources.title: The potential of payroll in 2026 Global payroll survey
sources.population: Senior payroll stakeholders at organisations with over 1000 employees across 20 countries
sources.published_date: 2026 edition; exact publication date not established
sources.locator: Printed pages 8 and 21; relevant sections inspected through web PDF reader
sources.summary: The report examines workforce capability, compliance, AI, integration and reporting. Its large-employer and multinational context matters. A stated integration barrier overlaps JGA's topic; it does not reconstruct individual approval cases.
sources.limitations: Country-specific bases and collection dates not located. Some integration-strategy wording needs clarification before numerical reuse. Local download returned HTTP 403; no local PDF capture is claimed.
sources.publication_eligibility: Working context or source-attributed finding; final wording and rights checks pending

sources.title: HR.com Future of Payroll 2025
sources.publisher: HR Research Institute / HR.com; hosted by IRIS
sources.population: HR professionals across industries and sizes, mostly North America
sources.locator: Printed pages 3 and 40 visually verified; relevant technology sections inspected
sources.summary: Desired missing features and payroll maturity are already surveyed. On page 40, customisability is 41% in prose but 37% in the chart, so that figure is held rather than resolved by preference.
sources.limitations: Mixed HR population is not UK senior payroll. Associations between maturity and outcomes are not causal effects.
sources.publication_eligibility: Working context or source-attributed finding; final wording and rights checks pending

sources.title: Payroll at the tipping point The case for C-suite elevation
sources.population: Senior leaders, according to the publisher landing page; full eligibility not inspected
sources.locator: Public report description and download/consent section
sources.summary: Executive ownership, governance, controls and fragmented payroll are already part of a current published research proposition. The public page reports a 319-leader survey; full method and report content were not inspected.
sources.limitations: Landing-page coverage only. Do not claim the full report was reviewed or use its unseen numbers. No download form submitted.
sources.publication_eligibility: Working context or source-attributed finding; final wording and rights checks pending

sources.title: The 2024/25 audit of the Scottish Government Consolidated Accounts
sources.publisher: Auditor General for Scotland / Audit Scotland
sources.population: Scottish Government public-sector Oracle shared HR/Finance implementation case
sources.summary: Provides an actual business-case and implementation history, a useful counterexample to claiming decision journeys have never been documented. Treat as one institutional case and distinguish combined programme scope from payroll alone.
sources.limitations: One public-sector shared HR/Finance implementation case; not payroll-only costs or employer prevalence.
sources.publication_eligibility: Working context or source-attributed finding; final wording and rights checks pending
